title_ar: الشيخ الددو ضيف شرف لحفل افتتاح المؤتمر الوطني السابع لحزب العدالة والتنمية المغربي
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Guest of Honour at the Opening Ceremony of the Seventh National Congress of the Moroccan Justice and Development Party
body_ar: افتتحت٬ صباح اليوم السبت 14 يوليو /2012 م بالعاصمة المغربية الرباط٬ أشغال المؤتمر الوطني السابع العادي لحزب العدالة والتنمية٬ تحت شعار "شراكة فعالة من أجل البناء الديمقراطي". ويحضر فضيلة العلامة الشيخ : محمد الحسن الددو بوصفه ضيف شرف لحفل افتتاح المؤتمر؛ ويستمر المؤتمر على مدى يومين وتحضره وفود كبيرة من داخل المغرب وخارجه. ويشارك في هذا المؤتمر 3300 مؤتمر٬ من ضمنهم 550 مشاركة٬ و1600 شاب٬ و83 عضوا يمثلون الجالية المغربية بالخارج ينتمون ل12 دولة. إلى ذلك عرف الحفل حضور عدد من الضيوف والشخصيات العالمية البارزة ، من بينهم رئيس المكتب السياسي لحركة حماس د. خالد مشعل، وأبو جرة سلطاني، والناشطة اليمنية توكل كرمان، وقيادات من حزب العدالة والتنمية والسعادة بتركيا، ومعن بشور ومنير شفيق وأحمد منصور.
body_en:
This morning, Saturday 14 July 2012, in the Moroccan capital Rabat, the proceedings of the Seventh Ordinary National Congress of the Justice and Development Party opened, under the banner "An Effective Partnership for Democratic Construction".

The eminent scholar Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew is attending as a guest of honour at the congress's opening ceremony. The congress runs over two days and is attended by large delegations from inside Morocco and from outside it.

Taking part in this congress are 3,300 delegates, among them 550 women participants, 1,600 young people, and 83 members representing the Moroccan community abroad, belonging to 12 countries.

In addition, the ceremony saw the attendance of a number of guests and prominent international figures, among them the head of the political bureau of the Hamas movement, Dr Khaled Meshaal; Abu Jerra Soltani; the Yemeni activist Tawakkol Karman; leaders from the Justice and Development Party and the Felicity Party in Turkey; and Maan Bashour, Munir Shafiq and Ahmed Mansour.

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12. The record is a bare attendance list and contains no statement by anyone; but it places the Sheikh, as guest of honour, at a platform also attended by the head of Hamas's political bureau — an organisation proscribed in a number of jurisdictions — and by other figures who have since become contested. Published in English it will be read as association rather than as the routine political reporting it is. Nothing has been omitted and no one has been described in terms the source does not use. The publication decision, and whether to carry the date prominently, belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

HOMONYM WARNING, of the kind a machine reading gets wrong. Unvocalised, مؤتمر is both muʾtamar, a conference, and muʾtamir, one who takes part in it. The second word of 'في هذا المؤتمر 3300 مؤتمر' is the participant, not the event. Rendered 'delegates'.

مشاركة with the feminine ending, counted among persons, is a woman taking part; the same form also means 'participation' as an abstract noun, which is how a literal reading goes wrong. The breakdown pairs it with 'young people' and 'members', confirming the personal sense. Rendered 'women participants'.

flags.note: The Arabic can be read as two Turkish parties — the AK Party (Adalet ve Kalkınma) and the Felicity Party (Saadet) — or as one body with a triple name, which does not exist. The two-party reading is adopted and the conjunction kept visible; a reviewer should confirm from contemporary coverage. Both Turkish parties are given the English names they use themselves rather than translations of the Arabic.

translator_notes: A news-desk report of a party congress, lifted in part from agency wording. It carries no words of the Sheikh's and no religious content whatever; his presence is the only reason it is in this corpus.
The CMS timestamp, 14 July 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body gives the same day for the opening.

Names of attendees are given in the forms usual in English-language coverage: Khaled Meshaal, Abu Jerra Soltani, Tawakkol Karman, Maan Bashour, Munir Shafiq, Ahmed Mansour. None has been identified beyond what the source says of them.
